text.p: Four young Norwegian neo-Nazis were held in custody on Saturday on suspicion of planning to use violence against the democratic state, news reports said.
The reports said police had found lists of politicians, including Prime Minister Thorbjoern Jagland, and other well-known leaders that the neo-Nazis may have planned to attack or assassinate.

The men, in their 20s, were rounded up near Oslo along with dynamite, bullet-proof vests and helmets -- but no weapons -- in a crackdown on neo-Nazis in the past few days, the reports said quoting security police officials.
A 49-year-old woman suspected of financing the alleged anti-state activity was arrested in the west coast city of Bergen on Friday, the reports said.
The national news agency NTB said police requested that the men be remanded in custody for four weeks while the investigation continued.
An Oslo court hearing on Saturday was inconclusive and a decision was postponed until Monday, NTB quoted police as saying.
The defendants, who can be sentenced to a maximum six years in prison if found guilty, pleaded not guilty, NTB said.
Ellen Holager Andenaes, head of the security police, was tightlipped about the case.

"The police believe that youngsters belong to a violent neo-Nazi group," she told NTB. "We believe we have arrested some rather central figures in this environment, but the investigation will show how big the case is."
Norwegian neo-Nazis, while small in numbers, have in the past few years met increasingly with Swedish, German and other neo-Nazis at rock concerts, experts on extremist groups say.

"They get inspiration abroad and maybe acquire a need to show themselves as tough people," sociologist Henrik Lunde told the daily Dagbladet. "For the first time it looks like (Norwegian) neo-Nazis have been planning to take action."
